title: Where did the note go?
hook: You search for a note you deleted yesterday.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Distinguish active-only search from including deleted items.

objective: Distinguish active-only search from including deleted items.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: You search for a note you deleted yesterday. The search lists active files. Is 'notes' in the list? Correct option: No, it is left out. Fixture files are stipulated.
claims.source: Stipulated exercise fixture in studyCatalog.ts. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 14), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).

claims.text: The note is marked as deleted. A search of active files leaves it out; including deleted items brings it back here. Real products keep deleted files for different lengths of time.
claims.source: Google Drive Help, Search for files in Google Drive, filtering and advanced search; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2375114?hl=en . claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: files. Exercise only; no measured productivity gain. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.

claims.text: If the file was deleted, a search of active files will keep missing it. Including deleted items can show it, within the product's own retention rules. Narrowing cannot find what the search leaves out.
